conventions.values: Engine-level decode output (DecodeSubrecord): FormIDs are "[XXXXXXXX]" as stored, localized strings "[LSTRING:0xXXXXXXXX]", byte runs upper-case hex, floats the float32 widened to double. Not skqe export output, which resolves FormIDs and nulls.
conventions.ctx: rt, fsig, form_version, localized, prev (the built-in $@Prev), vars (declared context variables by name, without the @), rectype (answers of the form-type resolver by stored FormID as 8 hex digits; null = no resolver).
conventions.field_vectors: Decode 'hex' with 'pattern' (and 'shared', 'options') under 'ctx'. Expect 'decoded' and 'tail_hex' (bytes after the pattern), or 'decode_error' (then the caller keeps the field raw). 'reencoded_hex' is what CaptureSubrecord followed by EncodeSubrecord plus the tail must give: always the input. 'encode_plain_hex' is EncodeSubrecord from the decoded value alone, with no events and the field size given; where 'encode_plain_differs' is true it is not the input and the note says why. 'pattern_before' / 'decoded_before' show today's catalogue entry and value for the same bytes.
conventions.encode_vectors: EncodeSubrecord of 'value' with no events; 'size' null means the field size is not known. Expect 'hex', or an error whose message contains 'error_contains'. Vectors with feature 'defaults' run with useDefaults on (spec I.1); all others with it off.
conventions.record_vectors: Walk 'fields' in order with one record context. For each field expect 'prev' and 'vars' as seen by its pattern, 'decoded' (or 'no_pattern'), and with a grammar 'slot' (index path into the grammar's fields, null when unplaced) and 'group' (instance path, "" at record level). 'expect_diagnostics' and 'expect_counts' are the matcher's and the count check's whole output, in order.
conventions.load_vectors: Load 'catalog_text'. 'format2' is the required result of the new loader; 'format1' is what today's loader does with the same text minus the $format key (shown so the difference is visible; 'n/a' where the text has no meaning in format 1).
conventions.error_text: Only error codes (load) and the overread flag (decode) are normative. Message text is given as a hint.
